previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, proteinuria, and a history of hepatitis C presented with a pain crisis involving her back, right leg, chest, and abdomen, likely triggered by dehydration from colonoscopy prep. She was treated with IV fluids and IV narcotics, with transition to oral pain medication as her symptoms improved. A PICC line was placed for reliable access. Chest imaging showed mild pulmonary vascular congestion but no acute chest syndrome or pneumonia. Despite anemia (hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL on discharge), she remained asymptomatic and was not transfused due to prior transfusion-related hepatitis C. Her pain resolved sufficiently for discharge, and she was sent home with an increased dose of hydroxyurea, instructions to follow up with her hematologist, and a plan to check a CBC within the week.
problems: Hb-SS disease with acute chest syndrome

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo F w/ history of Sickle Cell Disease c/b 
functional asplenia and recurrent pain crises presenting with L 
hip, back, and circumferential lower abdominal pain likely 
consistent with sickle cell pain crisis. 

ACTIVE:
#Sickle Cell Painful Episode 
Patient presented complaining of worsening lower back, abdominal 
and knee pain consistent with previous sickle cell crises. She 
denied all infectious symptoms. Patient was started on IVF and 
diluadid PO standing, with IV q3h PRN for breakthrough. She 
mostly used the PRN IV dilaudid and did not use much of PO 
dilaudid early in her admission, and her pain improved by day 2 
of admission. On the day of discharge patient's pain was 
reasonably controlled with transition to only PO dilaudid at her 
home dose. We continued her on her home meds, hydroxyurea and 
folic acid. She was persistently a little hypotensive with SBPs 
___, so we held her home Lisinopril. She received boluses 
of fluids when SBP <90, as well as maintenance fluids throughout 
her admission, but remained asymptomatic during these episodes. 
Chart review reveals she likely runs low at baseline. She was 
kept on a cycling automated BP monitor with frequent BP checks 
the night prior to discharge in order to watch her BPs more 
closely, and they remained stable. She presented with Hb 8.8 and 
dropped to 6.9 two days later (after receiving fluids). We 
wanted to transfuse at that time but patient refused due to 
history of HCV transmission via transfusion. Repeat CBC was 
reassuringly stable at 7.1. Patient had appropriate 
reticulocytosis, and evidence of chronic hemolysis secondary to 
sickle cell on labs with elevated indirect bilirubin and LDH. 
She remained afebrile without cough or chest pain throughout the 
admission. Incentive spirometer use was encouraged. Patient 
declined new script for PO dilaudid at discharge in favor of 
continuing home regimen with narcotic contract. She was 
ambulating without issue and had good PO intake prior to 
discharge.

CHRONIC:
#Osteosarcoma: Mass arose in L Tibia and was treated with 
resection and adjuvant chemotherapy. Soft tissue recurrence of 
osteosarcoma occurred in ___ and was treated with wide 
resection. Patient follows with orthopedics and has follow up 
appointment scheduled.

#HCV: Disease was acquired secondary to transfusion and 
consequently treated with Harvoni. Patient is followed by GI.

#History of microalbuminuria: Urine dipstick revealed negative 
protein, and home lisnopril held for lower BPs during 
hospitalization.
